text.en: A cheerful poem describes children playing in the garden on a fine day. They bounce, throw and catch a ball, tug, pull and fly a kite, and run, skip, jump, sway, slide and swing with friends. In this chapter you will learn new action words, use the joining word and, and make a paper bag puppet.

The poem is about children playing in the garden on every fine day. With a ball, they bounce it, throw it and catch it. With a kite, they tug it, pull it and fly it. With friends, they run, skip, jump, sway, slide and swing. Playing outdoors keeps us healthy and happy, but we must be careful so that we do not get hurt.
Bounce means to spring back up after hitting the ground, as a ball does. Throw means to send something through the air with your hand. Sway means to move slowly from side to side, like a branch in the wind. Slide means to move smoothly over a surface, like on a playground slide.
The poem has pairs such as run and skip, jump and sway, and slide and swing. The word and joins two words that go together. Give and take, sing and dance, eat and drink, catch and throw, run and catch are more pairs joined by and. We can think of our own pairs, such as read and write or sit and stand.
Children play many games, and the same game can have a different name in our mother tongue. When playing, we should take turns, play fairly and take care of ourselves and our friends.
You need a paper bag, a pencil, colour pencils or sketch pens, woollen thread and gum. Fold the base of the bag upward and hold it upside down. Draw the upper lip on the flap and the lower lip just below it, then draw a face and colour it. Slide your hand inside and bend your fingers, and the puppet can talk.

problem.en: What happens to a kite in the poem?

Then they fly it.
